transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what brought me in is I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to make time for things—painting, hiking, choir, and we’d have Sunday family gatherings, and I was usually the one reminding everyone, you know? My sister would always bring this terrible potato salad that somehow everyone still ate… sorry, that’s not really the point.

Now even if I have a free hour, I just sort of sit there. I can’t seem to care about any of it, even the things that used to matter to me.
Have you noticed a change in your interest or enjoyment in activities like painting, hiking, or spending time with your family and choir?

Yes… very much. I mean, I used to actually plan my week around those things—painting, getting out for a hike, choir practice, Sunday with everyone. I’d be the one texting people about what time to come, or reminding them who was bringing what.

Now, even if I have a free hour, I just… sit there. I think, “I could paint,” or “I should call my family,” and then it’s like I can’t make myself care enough to do it. It’s strange, because those things used to feel like me. Now they just feel far away.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… most days, honestly. It’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I’ll be in the classroom with students all around me, or even just sitting at home with my husband, and I still feel… hollow. Like I’m there, but not really there. And sometimes I’m just close to tears for no clear reason.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or do you feel more fatigued than usual, even if you haven't been doing much physically?

I’m not sure I’ve really paid attention to that specifically. I mean, I get tired, but… everyone gets tired, right? At school there’s always something going on, kids needing help, papers everywhere, someone’s glue stick rolling under a table—sorry, that’s probably not what you meant.

I don’t know if it’s more fatigue exactly. I just know I’m not doing much with the time I have. Whether that’s energy or something else, I’m not really sure.
Have you noticed that even small tasks, like getting ready for the day or walking to your car, feel more exhausting than they used to?

I don’t know… maybe? I haven’t really timed it or thought of it that way. Getting ready in the morning has never been my favorite thing anyway—there’s always some missing earring or I can’t find the sweater I meant to wear, and then I’m thinking about school and whether I remembered to put the reading folders back.

Walking to the car… I mean, it’s not far. So I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed that, exactly. It’s more like I just move through things without much… I don’t know. I’m not sure I can answer that very well.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, focus on tasks, or make decisions lately?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do misplace things sometimes, but I’ve always been a little like that—my husband jokes that I set my coffee down and then it becomes part of the furniture.

At school there are so many little interruptions, you know, someone needs help with a worksheet, then someone spills water, then the teacher asks me to photocopy something, so it’s hard to tell if I’m not focusing or if the day is just… like that.

Decisions… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed anything major, I guess. Nothing I could clearly point to and say, “That’s different.”
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Yeah… sleep has actually been kind of a mess. It’s been that way for months, I think.

I’ll get into bed and then my brain starts going over everything—like grant details and little things I should’ve remembered, and then somehow I’m thinking about whether I sent the right form or if I wrote something down in the wrong place. It’s ridiculous because it’s the middle of the night, I’m not going to fix anything then.

And then I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning and just… be awake. Sometimes I do sleep longer, but even then I get up feeling like I didn’t really sleep, like it didn’t count somehow.
Has there been a time recently when you felt no interest or pleasure in absolutely anything, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I think that’s actually the thing that finally made me come in. I don’t feel like myself anymore.

I used to paint, not anything fancy, just little things at the kitchen table, and I used to go hiking when the weather was decent. I sang in choir too, and Sundays with family used to feel like something I looked forward to. Now even if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I’ll think, “I could get the paints out,” or “I should call someone,” and then I just… don’t. It’s like I can’t make myself care about any of it.

And then I feel silly because people are busy, everyone gets tired, and my sister is always saying I should just come over anyway because once I’m there I’ll enjoy it, but I don’t know. It just doesn’t feel the same.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two years?

Most days, yes… I mean, I don’t know if I can neatly say “for two years” like marking it on a calendar. I’m not very good at that kind of thing—my husband remembers dates much better than I do.

But lately, most days, it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. Like I can be in the classroom with kids all around me, all that noise and activity, or sitting at home with my husband right there, and still feel completely hollow. Sometimes I’m just close to tears for no clear reason. It’s not always dramatic-looking from the outside, I don’t think, but inside it’s… it’s there most of the time.
Would you say that most days have felt depressed or down for you over the past two years, even if it wasn’t every single day?

Yes… most days, I’d say. I get a little caught on the “two years” part because I don’t keep track very neatly, but the feeling is there a lot.

It’s like this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in the classroom with all the students around me, or at home with my husband, and I still feel sort of hollow… like I’m not really in it. Sometimes I’m close to crying and there isn’t even a clear reason.
Would you say that you’ve had days like this—feeling down, hollow, or close to tears—more often than not over the past two years?

Yes… I think so. More often than not, anyway.

It’s like most days there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I’ll be in the classroom with students all around me, or at home with my husband, and I can still feel completely hollow, like I’m not really there. And then I’ll be close to tears over nothing in particular.

I mean, some days I can still function, I get through things, pack my lunch, answer emails—well, sometimes I forget the emails, but… yes. The feeling is there most days.
Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or depressed for at least two years, even if there were some better days in between?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. There are better days here and there, sure, like if the classroom is busy enough and I’m just moving from one thing to the next, or if my husband and I are doing something ordinary like grocery shopping—well, he always takes forever picking cereal, which drives me a little crazy—but even then, most days it’s like this heavy gray film is over everything.

I can be surrounded by students or sitting right next to my husband at home and still feel hollow. And sometimes I’m just close to tears, even when nothing specific has happened. So yes… persistently low, I think, most days.
Would you say that your low mood has been present more days than not for at least the past two years, even if there were some days when you felt a little better?

Yes… yes, I think that’s right. More days than not, it’s there.

It’s hard because I can still be doing normal things—standing in a classroom full of students, helping them with work, or sitting at home with my husband while he’s watching something—and I’ll still feel… hollow. Like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. Even if nothing bad is happening that day, I can feel close to tears.

Some days are a little lighter, I guess, but most days it’s there in the background.
